body.p: The following remarks are made in response to the Action. In this Response, claims 1 and 10 have been amended. No claims have been canceled or newly added. Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 remain pending. The claim amendments are supported by at least, for example, paragraphs [0051]-[0052] of the Specification as-filed. There is no new matter.

Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Applicant traverses the rejections. Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claims 1 and 10 have been amended accounting for the rejections. The claims are definite. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejections.
Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 stand rejected as being unpatentable over CN 208645329 ("Pei"). Applicant traverses the rejections.
Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to further recite:
a second arm link connected to the first hollow shaft, the second arm link
comprising:
a first stage reduction assembly extending along a second axis
thereof and coupled to a first power source of the robot;
a second stage reduction assembly ...
a third stage reduction assembly extending along a third axis
thereof and coupled to a second power source of the robot; and
a fourth stage reduction assembly comprising:

an input of the fourth stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of the third stage reduction assembly; and an output of the fourth stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of a second hollow shaft,
wherein the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the fourth stage reduction assembly; ...
a third arm link,

wherein the third arm link is coupled to the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly via the second hollow shaft, and wherein the third arm link is driven by the fourth stage reduction assembly via the second hollow shaft to rotate about a fourth
axis.

(Emphasis added.) The Action states that Pei teaches "a second arm link (20) connected to the first hollow shaft; a first stage reduction assembly ... a second stage reduction assembly (23, 24, 25) ... a third stage reduction assembly (planetary gearset resulting from the above modification to be between motor 11 and pulley 13) ... and a fourth stage reduction assembly (13, 14, 15)." (Action at pp. 4-5.) The Action also states that Pei teaches that "an output of the fourth stage reduction assembly (15) coaxially arranged on a periphery of a second hollow shaft (hollow shaft within 15), wherein the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage (via 14) with the input of the fourth stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of a third arm link (10) about a fourth axis (axis defined by 15 and hollow shaft therein)." (Action at p. 5.) For at least the following reasons, Pei does not teach the above recited features of amended claim 1.

Pei teaches that the "first cantilever 20" includes the "[s]econd cantilever drive device compris[ing] a servo motor 21, a second toothed belt transmission device and a hollow cycloidal reducer 22, the servo motor 21 is installed in the middle of the first cantilever 20, and the hollow cycloid reducer 22 is mounted on [t]he front end of the first cantilever 20." (Pei at p. 4 of machine translation.) Pei also teaches that the "first cantilever driving device [10] comprises a servo motor 11, a first toothed belt transmission device and a cycloidal-pin wheel speed reducer 12. (Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) See, for example, the annotated version of FIG. 2 of Pei below:

Moreover, Pei teaches that the "first tooth-shaped belt transmission device comprises a driving pulley 13, a toothed belt 14, and a driven pulley 15, a drive pulley 13 fixed on the servo motor 11 the shaft end; the driven belt wheel (15) is fixed on the hollow input shaft of the cycloidal pinwheel speed reducer 12." (Pei at
p. 3 of machine translation (emphasis added).) See, for example, the annotated version of FIG. 3 of Pei below:

Servo M SVG {EMBED HERE} 3.0774.727
(15)

In contradistinction, the "first cantilever 20" of Pei does not teach the "second arm link," as recited in amended claim 1, because the "first cantilever 20" of Pei does not include the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15." Instead, the "hanger 10" of Pei teaches including the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15."

For similar reasons as stated above, the "hanger 10" of Pei does not teach the "third arm link," as recited in amended claim 1, because the "hanger 10" of Pei includes the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15." Pei does not teach that the "hanger 10" is "coupled to the output of the "driven pulley 15." Instead, as shown above in annotated FIG. 2 of Pei, the "driven pully 15" of Pei is located in the "hanger 10," which is coupled to the "second hollow shaft 19." Therefore, Pei does not teach "a third arm link," and "wherein the third arm link is coupled to the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly via the second hollow shaft, and wherein the third arm link is driven by the fourth stage reduction assembly via the second hollow shaft to rotate about a fourth axis," as recited in amended claim 1.
Furthermore, the Action states that:
[I]f applicant amends toward this particular location of parts to be in the second arm link rather than a third arm link (distinct from the second), such

would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention for the purpose of moving the weight of these parts closer to the support base of the arm and thus reducing cantilever
forces and reducing the force necessary to drive the third arm link.
(Action at p. 6.) For at least the following reasons, a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) would not arrive at the features of amended claim 1 based on the teachings of Pei.

The "hanger 10" of Pei includes the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15." In addition, as stated above, the "driven pully 15" of Pei is located in the "hanger 10," and coupled to the "second hollow shaft 19," which is connected to "rear end 28" of the "first cantilever 20." (See Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.) Relocating the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15" from the "hanger 10" of Pei to the "first cantilever 20" of Pei would render the "hanger 10" incapable of connecting to the "second hollow shaft 19" of Pei, which would thereby render the "hanger 10" of Pei inoperable as the "hand drive device." (See Pei at p. 3 of machine translation.)

Pei also does not teach that the components from the "hanger 10" are located in the "first cantilever 20," because the "hanger 10," the "first cantilever 20," and the "second cantilever 30" of Pei includes their respective components therein such that the "four-joint robot" of Pei "does not occupy the space of the table surface, [and] the table space utilization rate is high." (Pei at p. 2 (emphasis added).) The Action as cited above states without providing any basis that Pei teaches relocating the components from the "hanger 10" of Pei including the "servo motor 11," the "drive pulley 13," the "toothed belt 14," and the "driven belt wheel 15" closer to the support base in the "first cantilever 20" of Pei. Accordingly, the Action's assertion that Pei teaches the "second arm link," as recited in amended claim 1, is conclusory and an exercise in impermissible hindsight reasoning. Therefore, the Action fails to establish a prima facie case of obviousness regarding the above recited features of amended claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2- 4, 6, 8, and 9 are patentable over Pei. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness
of the rejection with respect to features not discussed. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.

It is submitted that the rejections in the Action have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is solicited.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific allegation or comment of the Action does not signify agreement or concession with that part. Also, the arguments herein are not exhaustive. The amendment or cancelation of a claim or other part of the Specification does not necessarily signify concession with an allegation or comment of the Action. Applicant reserves the right to prosecute the rejected claims in further prosecution of this or related applications.
